mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a short-term discounting effect that reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during FEDFUNDS > 4% periods (p > 0.05), or the effect is reversed in subsequent months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer demand indicators (HOUST) creates a dual softening in labor market and demand conditions, predicting negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while HOUST decreases over the prior 2 months
regime_hint: labor market weakening coupled with weak demand
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during such dual weakening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month average signals accelerating business activity, which is expected to boost investor confidence and drive positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant correlation between INDPRO acceleration and 20-day forward returns (p > 0.10) in 6 consecutive expansionary months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in the RSAFS (residential and commercial absorption) accompanied by a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates supply-side softness that reduces growth expectations and predicts negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >10% while CPIAUCSL declines by >2% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and robust across 5 such contraction episodes (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the UNRATE falls below 6% for three consecutive months, it suggests labor market slackening that lowers real discount rates, supporting higher equity valuations and positive 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than average during such UNRATE conditions (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (employment increases) without a corresponding rise in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests labor market over-heating that can trigger a short-term bearish reaction in equities over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS jumps >20% while INDPRO remains flat in the prior week
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative or at least 10% below the prior 5-day average during such spikes.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) and weak demand (HOUST) indicate deflationary pressures that reduce growth forecasts and are associated with negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 208.0 and HOUST < 620.0 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the 3-month moving average of GDPC1 (real private demand) suggests a softening in economic activity that lowers growth expectations and predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns, regardless of FEDFUNDS stance.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative or at least 5% below the 12-month average during GDPC1 declines of similar magnitude.
